questions.qText: Calculate the number of moles present in 24.0 g of magnesium (Mg).
Calculate the mass, in grams, of 0.25 moles of carbon dioxide (CO2).
A student weighs out 17.0 g of ammonia (NH3). Calculate the number of moles of NH3 used.
What is the mass of 1.50 moles of sodium hydroxide (NaOH)?
Calculate the number of moles of oxygen atoms present in 8.0 g of sulfur trioxide (SO3).
A sample of an unknown gas has a mass of 4.4 g and contains exactly 0.10 moles. Calculate its relative molecular mass (Mr) and suggest its identity.
A student requires 0.050 moles of hydrated magnesium sulfate (MgSO4·7H2O). Calculate the exact mass of the hydrated crystals needed.
2.00 g of a Group 2 metal oxide (XO) contains 0.050 moles of the compound. Calculate the relative atomic mass (Ar) of the Group 2 metal X, and identify the metal.
Calculate the volume, in dm³, occupied by 0.75 moles of nitrogen gas (N2) at room temperature and pressure (r.t.p.).
A gas syringe collects 6.0 dm³ of chlorine gas (Cl2) at r.t.p. Calculate the number of moles of chlorine gas collected.
What is the volume, in cm³, of 0.015 moles of hydrogen gas (H2) at r.t.p.?
Calculate the mass of 2.4 dm³ of methane (CH4) gas at r.t.p.
Flask A contains 0.2 g of hydrogen gas (H2) and Flask B contains 1.6 g of methane gas (CH4). Both are at r.t.p. Determine which flask contains the larger volume of gas.
0.20 mol of solid calcium carbonate (CaCO3) is heated strongly until it completely decomposes. Calculate the maximum volume of carbon dioxide gas produced at r.t.p.
A student vaporizes a volatile liquid and collects 120 cm³ of its gas at r.t.p. If the mass of the gas collected is 0.30 g, calculate the relative molecular mass (Mr) of the volatile liquid.
A gas mixture contains 0.05 mol of oxygen (O2) and 0.15 mol of nitrogen (N2). Calculate the total volume, in dm³, of this gas mixture at r.t.p.
Calculate the concentration, in mol/dm³, of a solution containing 0.10 moles of sodium chloride (NaCl) dissolved in 0.25 dm³ of water.
A solution of nitric acid has a concentration of 0.20 mol/dm³. Calculate the number of moles of HNO3 present in 500 cm³ of this solution.
8.0 g of solid sodium hydroxide (NaOH) is dissolved in water to make exactly 500 cm³ of solution. Calculate the concentration of the solution in mol/dm³.
Convert a concentration of 0.25 mol/dm³ of nitric acid (HNO3) into g/dm³.
A commercial bottle of aqueous hydrochloric acid has a label stating its concentration is 7.3 g/dm³. Calculate its concentration in mol/dm³.
A student needs to prepare 500 cm³ of a 0.20 mol/dm³ aqueous sodium chloride (NaCl) standard solution. Calculate the exact mass of solid NaCl the student must weigh out.

In a titration, 20.0 cm³ of 0.15 mol/dm³ potassium hydroxide (KOH) is completely neutralized by 30.0 cm³ of sulfuric acid (H2SO4). Assuming a 2:1 molar ratio (KOH:H2SO4), calculate the concentration of the H2SO4 in mol/dm³.

25.0 cm³ of a 1.0 mol/dm³ copper(II) sulfate solution is transferred to a volumetric flask, and distilled water is added until the total volume reaches 250 cm³. Calculate the new concentration of the diluted solution in mol/dm³.
